defects.claim_says: The inserted date December 31, 1992 is 'unsupported as an actual end' because EO 12687 allows earlier extension and no held source records the committee's lapse; the end is EO 12869's revocation effective 1993-09-30.
defects.source_says: EO 12687 sec. 4(b) as amended by this order reads that the Committee 'shall terminate on December 31, 1992, unless sooner extended.' That is a self-executing sunset: the committee ended on that date by law unless an extension issued, and lapse needs no separate record. The claim's own search of EO 12687's number (EO 12687, 12741, 12785, 12869 and the OLRC note at 20 U.S.C. 1221) found no extension beyond 1992. EO 12869 Sec. 4 revokes EO 12687 among orders 'which established committees that have terminated or whose work is completed', which corroborates the lapse. The amendment's only content is the committee's run to 1992-12-31, so under the strike-and-insert and until-date rulings its first end is its own date, 1992-12-31 (inclusive). The 1993-09-30 revocation of the already-lapsed parent is a later event.

defects.claim_says: One clause, EO:12910#whole, whose original_operative_text and original_source (characters 1272 to 1653) are Sec. 2 only; the rationale states 'The dossier holds one clause (the whole order), which covers both sections.'
defects.source_says: In the held text (59 FR 21915), characters 1272 to 1653 hold only Sec. 2, the exception: 'Sec. 2. The first sentence of section 1 of this order shall not apply to those offices...'. Sec. 1, the operative closing command, lies before that span and is in no clause: 'All executive departments, independent establishments, and other governmental agencies, including their field services, shall be closed on April 27, 1994, ... That day shall be considered as falling within the scope of 5 U.S.C. 6103(b) ...'. The inventory omits the order's main command, and the rationale's statement that the clause covers both sections is false. The judgment_reason quotes 'shall be closed on', which is not in the clause's own text.

defects.claim_says: The parent's termination provision for the Commission, restated by later amending orders to October 3, 2001 ... is disclosed as a spent-fact candidate and the order stays on the books until the express revocation (citing the owner's 2026-10-21 reasoning)
defects.source_says: The 2026-10-21 report-deadline ruling covers report-relative endings and states 'a clause with its own fixed date is unaffected'. The parent's sunset is a fixed date: EO 13046 'NBAC shall terminate on October 3, 1999, unless extended by the President prior to that date', moved by EO 13137 sec. 3(c) to 'October 3, 2001'. No held extension exists, and EO 13316 lists the order among those that established committees that 'have terminated or whose work is completed'. The fixed own-terms sunset, 2001-10-03, is a dated earlier end that the claim dismisses on a ruling that excludes it. The claim does not resolve it, and 2003-09-30 is unsupported as the first end.

defects.claim_says: The restated termination date of October 3, 2001 is an earlier candidate: no held source shows an extension ... so under the owner's 2026-10-21 reasoning (the order stays on the books until revoked) it is disclosed as a spent fact and not recorded as the end; first end 2003-09-30
defects.source_says: This order's own section 3(c) sets the Commission's fixed termination: new section 8(b) is amended by deleting 'October 3, 1999' and inserting 'October 3, 2001' (the sentence as restated by EO 13046 reads 'NBAC shall terminate on ... unless extended by the President prior to that date'). The 2026-10-21 report-deadline ruling says 'a clause with its own fixed date is unaffected', so it does not support treating a fixed sunset as a spent fact. No extension is held, and EO 13316 recites that the listed committees 'have terminated or whose work is completed'. The fixed own-terms end of 2001-10-03 is not resolved; the 2003-09-30 first end for every clause, including section 3(c) itself, is unsupported.

defects.claim_says: No earlier end is held. The order states no period, date or condition. ... No held order revokes, supersedes or rewrites this order before EO 9830. unresolved_material_gaps: []
defects.source_says: The amended paragraph lists 'One general counsel' under Subdivision XL of Schedule A, the Board of Investigation and Research (FR contents on 7 FR 363; EO 9004 Schedule A 'XL. BOARD OF INVESTIGATION AND RESEARCH (Transportation Act of 1940)'). The held Transportation Act of 1940, 54 Stat. 898 (jobs/source-ladder text, sha256 f2592428...), section 306 provides: 'This part shall cease to have effect at the end of two years after its enactment unless extended by a proclamation of the President for an additional period which shall not exceed two years.' The Act was approved September 18, 1940, so the Board's statutory life ended no later than September 18, 1944 absent a further Act. That is a held, dated candidate for an earlier end (the position and its exception losing their object) that the claim neither cites nor resolves; the dossier's own prior review flagged it as material.

defects.claim_says: 1947-11-30, the outer limit, recorded as the best supported date because no earlier end is held
defects.source_says: The order exempts Summerlin "for such time as may be deemed necessary, but not beyond" Nov 30, 1947, so that date is only an upper bound. Public sources show the exemption ended earlier: Arlington National Cemetery records his death on 07/01/1947, and the Wikipedia biography gives his death as July 1, 1947 and his retirement as 1946. A personal exemption from retirement cannot outlast the person. The first end is therefore no later than 1947-07-01 and probably in 1946. Recording the outer limit treats missing evidence as proof of absence (owner ruling 2026-10-28, points 2-3). The claim needs the retirement or death date from a held source, or must stay open on that question.
